content.text: Section 22 satisfies every element of the preferred position, and no other audit/inspection right binds us.

input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
input.rationale: Section 22 is the only provision granting audit/verification rights against us (a document-wide search for audit, inspection, verification, monitoring, remote access and telemetry surfaced nothing else; § 23 contains only a heading). It matches the preferred position on every parameter: frequency limited to once in any twelve-month period, thirty days' prior written notice, normal business hours with no unreasonable disruption, off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality (§ 22.1); Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds five percent (§ 22.2); and Vendor and its auditor are expressly barred from direct access to Customer systems, unrelated Customer Data, privileged material and third-party confidential information (§ 22.2). Section 22.3 adds customer-favourable protections (findings are our Confidential Information, use limited to enforcement, copy of the final report, and shortfall payment resolves the issue). No redline needed.
